name: Gen (Mina)
notes: Gen (Gɛn, Gɛ̃gbe, Mina, Guin, Popo), a Gbe (Kwa) language of the Maritime Region of southeastern Togo and adjoining Benin, mutually intelligible with and sometimes classed as a dialect of Ewe. Same Africa-Alphabet-derived Latin orthography convention as Ewe: ɖ ƒ ɣ ŋ ɔ ɛ ʋ plus digraphs gb kp ny ts. Vowels a e ɛ i o ɔ u, with nasalised counterparts written with a following ⟨n⟩ (ã ẽ ɛ̃ ĩ õ ɔ̃ ũ), not modelled as separate graphemes here, matching the ee convention. Standardised in Benin's Alphabet des langues nationales (2008). TONE: Gen is tonal; the standard orthography is largely toneless like Ewe, so tone is not modelled here. Consonant/allophone inventory inherited from Ewe (`ee`) given the close genetic and orthographic relationship; graphemes stated independently here because Gen's own letter set and grapheme-to-phoneme values are directly attested.

ancestors.notes: Atlantic-Congo — the classification node this language sits under; Gbe (Kwa) has no dedicated clade node in this dataset yet, following the ee/fon convention of pointing straight at the Atlantic-Congo node.
Gen is mutually intelligible with Ewe and treated by some sources as an Ewe dialect; grapheme-to-allophone conventions closely track Ewe's.

location.notes: Maritime Region, southeastern Togo — the Gen/Mina-speaking area around Aného.
